text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Forest industry employers will not yet start separate pay deal negotiations with the paper workers' union, says Mauri Moren, deputy managing director at the Finnish Forest Industries Federation.
- Board of insurer Suomi to decide next autumn on the fate of its shares in insurer Pohjola, says Pohjola CEO Iiro Viinanen. @
- Finnish Museum of Modern Art is interested in buying the modern art collection now worth 20-30 million markka from the bankruptcy estate of former investor Pentti Kouri.
- Finnish pulp manufacturers do not have confidence in new pulp derivatives exchange, say it will not stabilise pulp prices, sector representatives say.
- Finland has not been fast enough in dismantling the monopoly status of state-owned Alko, European Commissoner for competition Karel Van Miert said during a visit to Finland. @
- Heavy taxation and a bloated public sector are not essential conditions for a high level of social security, results can be achieved also with lower expenses, finance ministry study says.
- Conditions exist for broad 1998 pay deal despite the paper union's decision to opt out, says Lauri Ihalainen, chairman of the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK).
- Aktia Bank managing director Johan Horelli says any talk of a merger between Aktia and the coop banks separated from OKObank would be unreal. @
- Increaing costs of medicine could be curbed by cutting or even abolishing value-added tax (VAT), Finnish Pharmacy Federation says.
- Only one line on security policy and NATO exists in the government, Defence Minister Anneli Taina says.
